draft.title: What a matrix is
card: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers in rows and columns. It stores information, such as sales figures in a table or the links between places in a network.
The order of a matrix is its number of rows × its number of columns. A matrix with 2 rows and 3 columns has order 2 × 3. Each number in it is an element.
a row matrix has one row, such as [4 7 9], which has order 1 × 3. A column matrix has one column.
a square matrix has equal numbers of rows and columns. A zero matrix has every element 0. An identity matrix is square, with 1s down the diagonal from top left and 0s elsewhere.
draft.remember: Order is rows × columns. A square matrix has equal rows and columns.

a.q: A matrix has 3 rows and 2 columns. What is its order?
a.why: Order is written as rows × columns, so 3 rows and 2 columns gives 3 × 2. The option 2 × 3 swaps the two numbers, which is the most common mistake.

b.q: Mia records the points of 4 players over 4 games in a matrix with 4 rows and 4 columns. Which type of matrix is this?
b.why: The number of rows equals the number of columns, so it is square. It would be an identity matrix only if it had 1s on the diagonal and 0s elsewhere, and points scored need not look like that.
b.clue: Compare the number of rows with the number of columns.
